description: Byte-exact snapshots of the authoritative texts the classifier's rules and fixtures rely on. Never edit a snapshot by hand; a new retrieval gets a new file and a new manifest entry.

sources.title: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 8 July 2026 amending Regulations (EU) 2024/1689, (EU) 2018/1139 and (EU) 2023/1230 as regards the simplification of the implementation of harmonised rules on artificial intelligence (Digital Omnibus on AI)
sources.text_status: Official Journal text: the XHTML rendition the Publications Office publishes of the electronic edition; the authentic edition is the signed PDF, which was not compared
relied_on_for: Art. 1(2)(a): Art. 2(2) AIA replaced (Annex I Section B products)
Art. 1(7)(a): Art. 5(1), first subparagraph, points (ba) and (bb) AIA inserted
Art. 1(40): Art. 113, third paragraph, points (a), (c) and (d) AIA
Art. 1(41): Annex I Section A point 1 deleted, Section B point 21 added
Art. 4: entry into force on the third day following publication

sources.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 13 June 2024 laying down harmonised rules on artificial intelligence (Artificial Intelligence Act)
sources.text_status: Official Journal text: the XHTML rendition the Publications Office publishes of the electronic edition; the authentic edition is the signed PDF, which was not compared; original version before Regulation (EU) 2026/1744
relied_on_for: Art. 2 (scope), Art. 5, Art. 6 and Annex I in their original wording
Art. 111(3): GPAI models placed on the market before 2 August 2025 comply by 2 August 2027 (not amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744)
Art. 113, third paragraph, point (b): Chapter V applies from 2 August 2025 (not amended)

sources.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, consolidated version 02024R1689 EN 27.07.2026 001.001 (amended by M1 Regulation (EU) 2026/1744)
sources.text_status: Consolidated version: a documentation tool with no legal effect; used only to cross-check the amended wording against the two Official Journal texts
relied_on_for: Cross-check of Art. 2(2), Art. 5(1)(ba), (bb), (1a), (1b), Art. 6(1a) to (1c), Art. 50(2), Art. 60a, Art. 111, Art. 113 and Annex I as amended
sources.notes: A query of the Publications Office SPARQL endpoint on 2026-10-14 returned only 02024R1689-20240712 and 02024R1689-20260727 as consolidated versions, and only 32026R1744 as an act amending 32024R1689.

sources.title: Directive 2011/93/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council of 13 December 2011 on combating the sexual abuse and sexual exploitation of children and child pornography, and replacing Council Framework Decision 2004/68/JHA
sources.text_status: Official Journal text as published; the heading of this rendition reads 'DIRECTIVE 2011/92/EU', while CELEX 32011L0093 and Art. 5(1)(bb) AIA refer to Directive 2011/93/EU. Four corrigenda (32011L0093R(01) to R(04)) are recorded in Cellar and were not read
relied_on_for: Art. 2, points (c) and (e): the material and performance referred to in Art. 5(1), first subparagraph, point (bb) AIA
Art. 5(1): conduct punishable when committed 'without right'
sources.notes: A query of the Publications Office SPARQL endpoint on 2026-10-14 found no act amending or repealing 32011L0093.

sources.title: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2026/2274 of 12 October 2026 on the harmonised standards for high-risk AI systems drafted in support of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 of the European Parliament and of the Council
sources.text_status: Official Journal text: the XHTML rendition the Publications Office publishes of the electronic edition; the authentic edition is the signed PDF, which was not compared
relied_on_for: Annex point 1: harmonised standard EN 18286:2026 (Artificial intelligence – Quality management system for EU AI Act regulatory purposes)

Art. 1 and recitals 1 to 6: publication of the reference of EN 18286:2026 in the Official Journal, which under Art. 40 AIA confers a presumption of conformity with the requirements the standard covers; recital 3 names quality management systems for providers of AI systems, including post-market monitoring processes, and the Decision does not name the AI Act articles concerned
Recitals 2 and 3: standardisation request C(2025) 3871, Annex I point 9

eurlex_check: Each snapshot was compared with the EUR-Lex rendition at eurlex_check.url on the date given, with the method scripts/compare_sources.py implements. The renditions differ in presentation only: EUR-Lex adds meta tags and stylesheet links in the <head>, appends scripts to the <body>, rewrites link and image targets and adds a class to some tables. Two forms of each are identical: the body text (head, scripts, styles and markup removed, character references resolved, whitespace collapsed; text_sha256) and the structure (the body's element names and text nodes in order, without attributes; structure_sha256). eurlex_bytes and eurlex_sha256 identify the EUR-Lex response that was compared. The Publications Office response itself was not fetched again, so sha256 is still the digest recorded at retrieval. Both sides are renditions the Publications Office serves; the authentic edition of the Official Journal, the signed PDF, was not compared.
